8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":10,"verseId":8,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Fire and Fuel","totalVerses":16,"verseData":{"id":"v10_8","number":8,"title":"The Priority Problem","sanskrit":{"text":"","transliteration":"","translation":"If fire depends on fuel, And fuel depends on fire, On what are fire and fuel established as dependent? Which one is established first?"},"philosophy":{"insight":"New phase: mutual dependence. If fire depends on fuel AND fuel depends on fire, which is established first? Neither can ground the other because each requires the other for its own establishment. The circularity prevents inherent establishment.","madhyamaka":"Mutual dependence under inherent existence creates a priority problem: to establish fire, you need fuel already established; to establish fuel, you need fire already established. Neither can be the first, inherently independent term in the relation.","quantum":"The measurement problem: the observed system's state depends on the measurement, and what counts as a measurement depends on the system. Observer and observed are interdependent — neither can be established independently before their interaction.","bridge":"Both QM's measurement problem and Nāgārjuna's fire-fuel expose circular interdependence where neither term can be independently established first. The circularity points to the absence of inherent, independent foundations.","accessible":"Which came first: the chicken or the egg? If each requires the other, neither can be \"first.\" Fire and fuel face the same problem: fire needs fuel, fuel needs fire. No starting point.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, fire and fuel arise together through conditions — no priority is needed. The problem arises only when we demand INHERENT establishment, which requires one to be independently prior.","commonMisconception":"NOT denying mutual dependence. Showing that mutual dependence is INCOMPATIBLE with inherent existence, which requires independent establishment."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Measurement Problem and Observer-Observed Interdependence","score":77,"strength":"High","explanation":"In QM, the measurement outcome depends on the system, and the system's state is defined relative to the measurement. Neither is independently established. Nāgārjuna shows the same for fire and fuel: neither can be the independent foundation for the other.","caveat":"The measurement problem is a specific issue in QM interpretation. The parallel is about circular interdependence preventing independent establishment."},"animation":{"visualBridge":"Two arrows in a circle: Fire → depends on → Fuel → depends on → Fire. No starting point, no independent foundation.","educationalGoal":"User sees that mutual dependence prevents either fire or fuel from being independently established first."},"deeperDive":[{"q":"Why does mutual dependence create a priority problem?","a":"Inherent existence requires independent establishment — each thing must be able to exist on its own, prior to its relations. But if A depends on B and B depends on A, neither can exist independently. The circle has no entry point.","realLifeExample":"A resume requires experience, but experience requires a job, which requires a resume. Without an entry point, the cycle can't begin \"inherently.\""},{"q":"How does fuel depend on fire?","a":"Fuel is only \"fuel\" (combustible material) in relation to fire. Without the concept/reality of fire, a log is just wood, not fuel. \"Fuel-ness\" is a relational property that depends on fire, just as fire depends on fuel to burn.","realLifeExample":"A \"student\" is only a student in relation to a teacher. Without teaching, there are no students. The identity is relational."},{"q":"How does the measurement problem parallel this?","a":"In QM: what the system IS depends on how it's measured. What counts as a measurement depends on the system. Observer and observed are circularly interdependent. Neither has an independently established state prior to their interaction.","realLifeExample":"A question shapes the answer, but the answer reveals what the question really asked. They define each other in the interaction."},{"q":"Isn't conventional mutual dependence fine?","a":"Yes! Conventional mutual dependence is Nāgārjuna's own view: fire and fuel arise together, defining each other conventionally. The PROBLEM is trying to make this work under inherent existence, which demands independent, prior establishment of at least one term.","realLifeExample":"Two friends define each other as friends — conventionally fine. But if each \"inherently\" needs the other to exist first, you get a paradox."},{"q":"Does this refute all dependence?","a":"No — it refutes INHERENT dependence (dependence between inherently existing things). Conventional, empty dependence — where neither term has inherent existence — avoids the priority problem entirely because no independent establishment is required.","realLifeExample":"Two mirrors facing each other create infinite reflections — neither reflection is \"first.\" But the mirrors (conventionally) are set up by conditions. No inherent priority needed."},{"q":"How does v.8 set up vv.9-12?","a":"V.8 poses the priority question. V.9 examines asymmetric dependence (fire on fuel). V.10 examines circular dependence. V.11 critiques dependence itself. V.12 concludes with the tetralemma: neither dependent nor independent.","deeper":"The dependence analysis (vv.8-12) is the most sophisticated part of the chapter. It shows that even the seemingly reasonable \"middle\" position — interdependence — can't work under inherent existence. Only EMPTY interdependence succeeds."}],"quiz":{"beginner":{"question":"What problem does mutual dependence create under inherent existence?","options":["A) No problem","B) Neither fire nor fuel can be established first — each requires the other, creating an unresolvable circle","C) Fire is always first","D) Fuel is always first"],"correct":"B","explanation":"Inherent existence requires independent establishment.
